info.title: Ticket Fairy public API
info.summary: Live events on Ticket Fairy, readable without a credential.
info.description: The event listing is public and needs no API key. Reads that return a person's data, and every write, need a credential: see https://www.ticketfairy.com/auth.md. Prices, fees and availability change, so read the live event page or this API for anything a user will pay for rather than quoting a cached copy. Version 1 changes only by addition. A retirement is announced with the Deprecation and Sunset headers at least 6 months ahead: see https://www.ticketfairy.com/api/v1/versioning.md. The organiser operations need a Bearer token. For your own scripts, create a Personal Access Token in your account settings (https://manage.ticketfairy.com/account). For an AI agent that acts for a person, see https://www.ticketfairy.com/auth.md. The token carries the person's role, so it reaches only the brands and events they can reach. Send Accept: application/vnd.api+json on every organiser request: without it, some addresses go to an older API that answers 400 NOT_LOGGED_IN. Responses carry Content-Type: application/json.

get.description: Public events that are on sale or upcoming, newest on-sale first by default. Filter by a search term, a country, a region, a date window or a listing section, and page through the result with `pagination.nextCursor`. No credential.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Words to find. With the default sort by start date, the words are matched as whole words, with tolerance for typos, in the event name, brand, venue, city and short description. With `sort=created_at` or `sort=updated_at`, or while the search index cannot answer, any part of the event, brand or venue name matches.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Only events in this country, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only events in this region, state or province.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Only events starting on or after this date.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Only events starting on or before this date.

parameters.name: section_type
parameters.description: Which listing section to read.

parameters.name: timezone
parameters.description: Interpret the date window and report dates in this IANA timezone.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to order by.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Ascending or descending.

parameters.name: brandId
parameters.description: Only events from this brand.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Which kinds of event to include, comma separated. All kinds when omitted.

schema.description: Comma-separated values from: activities, paid_events, free_events, external_events.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Which page of results, starting at 1. For reading page after page, prefer `cursor`.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: How many events per page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `pagination.nextCursor` value from the previous response, to read the next page. Send it with the same filters as that request. It sets the page and the page size, so `page` and `size` are ignored.

post.summary: Get several events in one request
post.description: A bulk read: up to 25 public events by their event links or slugs, in one request, instead of one request for each. Each link gets its own result, in the order sent: `found` with the event, `not_found`, or `invalid_link`. One unknown link does not fail the others. The same visibility rules as the listing apply. Read-only, so a retry is safe. No credential.

200.description: One result for each link sent.

post.description: Create an event for a brand you manage. Send flagDraft true to save a draft with only a name. To create a complete event, send its dates, sales end date, currency and venue. Send an Idempotency-Key so that a retry after a network error does not create a second event. Send Accept: application/vnd.api+json.

400.description: The Idempotency-Key is longer than 255 bytes.

403.description: You do not have the admin or owner role on this brand.

410.description: This Idempotency-Key was already used with a different body or endpoint. Use a new key.

422.description: The request is not valid, for example a missing field, a name with a blocked word, or an online event, which cannot be created here. The message names the first problem.

429.description: Too many events were created from this address, or a request with the same Idempotency-Key is still running. Wait for the number of seconds in Retry-After. After a rate limit, send the request again with a new Idempotency-Key.

get.description: Tickets sold and revenue for an event you can see, by day, and by ticket type and release. Ask for the sections you need with section; sales|release_breakdown returns both. A promoter sees only the sales they made. Send Accept: application/vnd.api+json.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: The event ID.

parameters.name: section
parameters.description: The report sections to return, separated by |. The sections for sales are sales and release_breakdown.

403.description: You cannot see this event's statistics.

422.description: A section name is not valid. The message lists the valid ones.

get.summary: Find an event to copy from
get.description: The events of the same brand that you manage and can copy into this one, at most 20. Without search, the brand's earlier events, with the likely previous edition first and named in suggested_id. With search, the brand's events whose name contains it, of any date. Send the chosen event_id as source_event_id to previewSetupCopy and startSetupCopy. Send Accept: application/vnd.api+json.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: The event ID.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Words in the name of the event to copy from.

200.description: The events you can copy from.

403.description: The brand does not have the Event Management feature, or you do not have the owner, admin or producer role on this event.

429.description: More than 120 requests were sent in a minute. Wait for the number of seconds in Retry-After.

get.description: What a copy from source_event_id would do, part by part, without copying anything: what it would add, what this event already has and keeps, what it would leave out and why, and whether the part can be copied at all. Show it to the person before startSetupCopy, and send the parts they choose. When active_run is not null, a copy is already running: follow it with getSetupCopyRun. Send Accept: application/vnd.api+json.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: The event ID.

parameters.name: source_event_id
parameters.description: The event to copy from, from listSetupCopySources.

400.description: source_event_id is missing or is this event (source_invalid).

403.description: The brand does not have the Event Management feature, or you do not have the owner, admin or producer role on this event or the event to copy from (not_allowed).

404.description: No event has this ID (event_not_found), or the event to copy from is not an event of the same brand (source_not_found).

post.description: Copy the setup of another event of the same brand, usually the previous edition, into this event, such as its stages, departments and rota. The copy runs in the background: the answer is 202 while it is queued or running, with the run in the body and its address in the Location header. Find the event to copy from with listSetupCopySources, and show the person what will change with previewSetupCopy first. GET that address until the status is done, partly_done or failed. The brand needs the Event Management feature, and you need the owner, admin or producer role on both events. Send Accept: application/vnd.api+json.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: The event ID.

202.description: The copy is queued or running. Follow it at the Location address.

200.description: The copy is not running, in one of two cases. This request_key was already used for the same copy and that copy has finished: the body is that run. Or the copy could not be queued: the status is failed with error_code not_started, nothing was copied, and allowed_actions.copy_again is true, so start it again later with a new request_key.

400.description: The request_key is missing or not 8 to 64 letters, digits, hyphens or underscores (request_key_required), a part name is not valid (parts_invalid), or the event to copy from is this event (source_invalid).

403.description: The brand does not have the Event Management feature, or you do not have the owner, admin or producer role on this event or the event to copy from (not_allowed).

404.description: No event has this ID (event_not_found), or the event to copy from is not an event of the same brand (source_not_found).

409.description: This request_key was already used for a different copy (request_key_reused), or a copy into this event is still running (copy_in_progress). data is that earlier run. For copy_in_progress, follow it, then start again.

429.description: More than 20 start requests were sent in a minute, whether or not they started a copy. Wait for the number of seconds in Retry-After.

get.description: One run of a setup copy, at the address the start answered with in Location. While the status is queued or running, wait a few seconds and GET it again. Send Accept: application/vnd.api+json.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: The event ID.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: The run ID, from data.id of the start.

200.description: The run as it is now.

403.description: The brand does not have the Event Management feature, or you do not have the owner, admin or producer role on this event.

404.description: No event has this ID, or this event has no run with this ID.

Pagination.description: Where this page sits in the result. To read the next page, send `nextCursor` as the `cursor` parameter with the same filters.

nextCursor.description: An opaque token for the next page. Null on the last page.

Event.description: One live event, exactly as the listing sends it. Start and end dates are ISO 8601 in the event's own timezone, which is given alongside them.

url.description: The public event page. The slug is the event's identity; keep it whole.

minimumAge.description: Digits as a string, for example "18".

startingPrice.description: The lowest price a buyer can pay now for a ticket type sold online to anyone, as the event page shows it. Null when nothing is on sale or the event is free. Null for an event with only free tickets or none on sale online. A guide, not a quote: checkout confirms the price.

createdAt.description: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS, with no timezone offset.

updatedAt.description: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS, with no timezone offset.

amount.description: The amount in major units, written with the currency's number of decimal places: "25.00" is 25 US dollars.

Currency.description: The currency tickets are sold in.

decimal_places.description: Minor-unit digits, normally an integer. An event saved with a numeric string keeps it, because the organiser API accepts any numeric value.

Brand.description: The organiser. Both fields are null when the event has no brand.

Venue.description: Where the event takes place. When hidden is true the name is null and the address fields are absent; the city, state and country stay.

ErrorResponse.description: The error body of this API. An address that no endpoint answers returns this body with status 404 and `code` `not_found`.

message.description: What went wrong, in plain language.

code.description: A stable error code to branch on, such as `invalid_parameter`, `rate_limited`, `not_found` or `listing_unavailable`.

hint.description: What to change before the next request.

parameter.description: The query parameter to correct, on a validation error.

retry_after.description: Seconds to wait before the next request, on a rate-limit error.

events.description: Event links, such as `https://www.ticketfairy.com/event/summer-festival`, or their slugs, such as `summer-festival`.

request.description: The link as it was sent.

message.description: Why there is no event, in plain language.

OrganiserEventAttributes.description: With flagDraft true, only displayName and slug are checked, when sent. Otherwise startDate, endDate, salesEndDate, currency and venue are required. An online event cannot be created through this API, so send a venue. Any other event attribute the dashboard uses may also be sent.

flagDraft.description: true saves a draft. It must be the JSON value true, not a string.

slug.description: The event address. It must be unique.

startDate.description: When the event starts. ISO 8601, read as UTC unless it has an offset, for example 2026-10-01T20:00:00Z.

endDate.description: When the event ends, after startDate. ISO 8601, read as UTC unless it has an offset, for example 2026-10-01T20:00:00Z.

salesStartDate.description: When ticket sales open, on or before startDate. ISO 8601, read as UTC unless it has an offset, for example 2026-10-01T20:00:00Z.

salesEndDate.description: When ticket sales close, on or before endDate. ISO 8601, read as UTC unless it has an offset, for example 2026-10-01T20:00:00Z.

timezone.description: An IANA timezone, for example Europe/London.

country.description: The country name, for example United Kingdom.

owner.description: The brand the event belongs to. You need the admin or owner role on it.

OrganiserSalesDay.description: Tickets sold on one day, in the event's timezone, for one currency. Box office sales are on separate rows. Numbers may arrive as strings. Money amounts are in the currency named. The money fields are left out for a role with limited statistics.

order_datetime.description: The first order of the day.

boxOfficePayment.description: 1 for sales at the box office.

grossIncome.description: Revenue including fees paid by buyers, less refunds.

pendingToPay.description: Still to be paid on payment plans.

release_breakdown.description: Sales and stock for each ticket type and release.

message.description: What went wrong, and what to change.

source_event_id.description: The event to copy from, usually the previous edition. It can be any other event of the same brand that you manage. listSetupCopySources lists them.

parts.description: What to copy. Leave it out to copy everything. A part you leave out is not copied: a part that needs it uses the matching items this event already has, and leaves out the items that have no match. Forms need the owner or admin role on both events: for a producer the forms part fails with needs_owner_or_admin and the run ends partly_done, so a producer leaves forms out.

request_key.description: A unique value you choose for this copy, such as a UUID. Sending the same key and the same choice again returns the same run, so a retry does not copy twice.

status.description: queued and running mean the copy is still going: GET the run again. done, partly_done and failed are final.

parts.description: Each part chosen, with how many items were copied, kept because this event already had them, and left out.

day_offset.description: Days between the two events, used to move copied dates.

copy_again.description: true when the copy has finished without copying everything, so starting it again with a new request_key can copy the rest.

suggested_id.description: The likely previous edition of this event, or null when there is none.

events.description: Events you manage that can be copied from, the suggested one first.

day_offset.description: Days between the two events. Copied dates move by this much.

parts.description: What each part would do. Nothing is copied by the preview.

key.description: Send it in parts to copy this part.

depends_on.description: Parts this one needs. Left out, this part uses the matching items the event already has.

mode.description: add_missing adds what this event is missing; only_when_empty copies only when this event has none.

kept.description: Items this event already has, which stay as they are.

left_out.description: Items left out, counted by reason.

examples.description: Names of some items it would add.

unavailable.description: Why the part cannot be copied at all, such as needs_owner_or_admin, or null.

suggested.description: true when the part would add something and can be copied.

active_run.description: A copy into this event that is still running, or null. Follow it before starting another.

error.description: What went wrong, and what to do.

OrganiserFeatureGateError.description: The brand does not have the feature this operation needs.

OrganiserSetupCopyError.description: A refusal of the copy, with error and code; a check before the copy, such as a missing event or a role, with message; or the Event Management feature check, with error only.

OrganiserBearer.description: A Personal Access Token, or an OAuth access token from https://www.ticketfairy.com/auth.md. Send it as Authorization: Bearer <token>.

OrganiserOAuth.description: Delegated access for an app or AI agent that acts for a person. The person signs in and approves the app; the token carries their role. Use PKCE with S256. The endpoints are the ones https://www.theticketfairy.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server publishes, and https://www.ticketfairy.com/auth.md describes the other ways an agent can get a token.

scopes.profile: Act for the person who approves the app, with their role.

OrganiserIdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
OrganiserIdempotencyKey.description: A unique value you choose for this request, such as a UUID, of at most 255 bytes. If you send the same key again with the same body within 24 hours, the first response is returned again, with the Idempotent-Replayed header, and the event is not created twice. That includes a 4xx response: after a 400, 403, 422 or a rate-limit 429, send the corrected request with a new key. A 5xx response does not keep the key, so you can retry with it. Keys are per account and not case-sensitive. The key 0 is ignored, so send any other value.

OrganiserRateLimitPolicy.description: The limit for creating events: 120 requests an hour for each client address.

OrganiserUnauthenticatedRateLimitPolicy.description: The budget for requests without a valid token: 300 requests a minute for each client address. Past it the answer is still 401, with Retry-After.

OrganiserRateLimit.description: Requests left in the current window (r) and seconds until it resets (t).

OrganiserIdempotentReplayed.description: Present, with the value true, when this is the stored response to an earlier request with the same Idempotency-Key.

OrganiserRetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before sending the request again.

OrganiserSetupCopyRateLimitPolicy.description: The limit for starting a setup copy: 20 requests a minute for each person.

OrganiserSetupCopyLocation.description: The address of this run, /api/event/{eventId}/setup-copy/runs/{runId} with the IDs filled in. GET it to follow the copy.

OrganiserWWWAuthenticate.description: A Bearer challenge, with resource_metadata pointing at the OAuth protected resource metadata.
